pages.text: "I'll just finish this row!" Dingding pulled weeds between the young rice plants. The sky darkened, and thunder rumbled far away. Mom, who worked several paddies on her own, looked down from the higher paddy.
Mom stepped onto the bank and called, "That was thunder! I'm coming out, too. Come quickly!" "Just a moment! I haven't finished this row." Dingding bent down and pulled more weeds.
Flash! A white crack split the dark sky. Rumble, boom! Dingding startled and sat down suddenly. The ducks below quacked and rushed into their house.
Mom reached from the bank, took Dingding's hand, and pulled them up. "You're the tallest thing in this paddy. Let's go home." They hurried along the bank to the doorway.

Mr. Ming, who kept ducks in the lowest paddy, came up to the doorway, too. "Don't stay in the paddy when you hear thunder. When Thunder Rumbles, Go Home!" They sat together as rain streamed across the empty paddies.
"One, stop what you're doing! Two, hold a grown-up's hand and leave the paddy! Three, wait inside!" Mr. Ming held up his fingers one by one. Dingding kept their knees together and nodded.
Another flash, then rumble, boom! Dingding was not startled now, because Mom was beside them. "When Thunder Rumbles, Go Home!" The three watched rain falling on the paddies from the doorway.
After a while, the sounds stopped and the sky brightened. Dingding sniffed the rich smell of rain-soaked soil. Their tightly clasped hands opened wide. Dingding was no longer afraid.
The next day, thunder rumbled again. Dingding called first, "One, stop playing! Two, hold a grown-up's hand! Three, go inside!" Dingding reached the doorway before Mom.
Mom stroked and patted Dingding's back. "You came in so well." When thunder rumbles, leave your play and come home. Dingding tapped their feet in the doorway. "When Thunder Rumbles, Go Home!"
